subject: Request: temporary inflight concurrency shield & throughput assurance for Oceanic Energy holiday campaign
messages:
From: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@oceanic-energy.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@oceanic-energy.com
Date: 2026-07-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Outbound holiday campaign — temporary inflight concurrency protection request

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Quick context: Oceanic is launching a targeted holiday marketing push the week of Nov 22 — expected burst of user inference traffic for our recommender and personalized messaging flows. We currently have a Reserved GPU commit with you, but our ops team is concerned about tail-queueing behavior when we hit sustained spikes (short bursts at 10–15x baseline over ~45 minutes).

Request: can Redwood provide a temporary "inflight concurrency shield" (policy that protects a slice of reserved capacity from preemption and aggressive queueing) for the campaign window, plus an explicit throughput assurance (tokens/sec range or equivalent) and acceptance criteria for queueing tail latency (95/99th percentile)? We need this in writing to justify a procurement amendment and fast-track an addendum with Legal.

Attached: capacity_report_Q2.pdf (summary of our usage), traffic-forecast.csv (projected bursts).

Appreciate a feasibility note and rough timelines — we need to sign an amendment by 2026-08-05 to lock marketplace windows.

Thanks,
Marcus Hale
Head of Platform Integrations
Oceanic Energy

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@oceanic-energy.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound holiday campaign — temporary inflight concurrency protection request

Marcus — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. Looping David (SRE/runtime) to validate queueing behavior and Ben to tee up commercial amendment options.

Quick answers up front: 1) We can design a short-term carveout to preserve a headroom slice of reserved GPUs for your campaign, 2) We can publish a short acceptance criteria statement with latency percentiles tied to the carveout, and 3) we will need exact traffic shape (per-minute qps and percentiles) so David can size the headroom.

David / Ben — can you confirm (a) technical feasibility in our Dedicated pool for a 72-hour window, (b) proposed quant (tokens/sec or concurrency units) to guarantee 95/99th latency, and (c) what contract wording + DocuSign flow we need to push the amendment by 2026-08-05?

Next step for Marcus: if you can confirm the peak qps and planned start/end datetimes (and whether you want a gradual ramp vs single-cut flag), I’ll coordinate the amendment and runbook.

— Lauren
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@oceanic-energy.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T13:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound holiday campaign — temporary inflight concurrency protection request

Hey all — technical note from runtime/SRE perspective.

Summary: we can implement a temporary headroom reservation for Oceanic's Dedicated pool that behaves like a protected lane (will not be preempted by autoscaler reclaim logic during the window). This is effectively a short-term reservation of N concurrency tokens mapped to your reserved GPUs.

Options and trade-offs:
- Option A (fastest): reserve a fixed concurrency shield (e.g., 120 concurrent inference slots) tied to your existing reserved nodes for the 72-hour window. Minimal code changes; we apply routing tags and priority queue. Expected deployment: 24–36 hours to validate and flip.
- Option B (elastic shield): allow a small burst headroom with step-scaling (50% extra for first 30 minutes, +25% next hour) with automatic rollback. More safety but needs 48–72 hours of tuning.

Metrics we need from Oceanic to size properly:
1) expected 1-min peak QPS, 2) typical tokens per request (mean/95th), 3) acceptable 95th/99th tail latency in ms for a single request, 4) window start/end UTC.

Acceptance criteria proposal: during the protection window our SLA will guarantee that 95th percentile token latency stays < X ms and that queueing backlog does not exceed Y seconds for more than Z consecutive minutes. (We will fill X/Y/Z once we have the traffic sample.)

Runbook notes: will ship a prewarm + canary traffic test (10–15% of projected peak) 2 hours before start, and an emergency rollback that relinquishes headroom if we detect unexpected interference with other tenants.

Risks: if bursts are heavily spiky with very large inference sizes, effective throughput is dominated by model KV-cache hotness; we may suggest a small model-variant (fp16/quant) for the campaign to reduce tail.

I’ll draft the technical addendum language and include the migration runbook link below.

— David
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@oceanic-energy.com>
To: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@oceanic-energy.com
Date: 2026-07-29T15:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound holiday campaign — temporary inflight concurrency protection request

Thanks David — this is exactly the level we need. Quick answers to your sizing questions below and confirming timeline:

1) 1-min peak QPS: 1,800 requests/min (30 rps peak sustained bursts ~45 minutes)
2) tokens per request: mean 220 tokens, 95th 620 tokens
3) acceptable tail latency: 95th < 350 ms, 99th < 700 ms
4) window: 2026-11-22T19:00:00Z to 2026-11-25T03:00:00Z (we want a 12-hour warmup on Nov 22)

We prefer Option A for predictability, but would consider Option B if you recommend it after sizing. Also — yes, please provide the addendum language. Procurement would like a one-paragraph assurance we can attach to our PO that states the temporary carveout and rollback conditions.

I can sign a short DocuSign amendment if you provide the link by Aug 3.

Best,
Marcus

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@oceanic-energy.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@oceanic-energy.com
Date: 2026-07-30T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Oceanic temporary reservation + next steps

Marcus — thanks for the numbers and the clear window. Summarizing action items and timeline so procurement/legal have a single place to reference: 

1) Technical: David will reserve an Option A headroom of 120 concurrency slots mapped to your reserved GPUs for 2026-11-22T07:00:00-08:00 PST (12-hour warmup) through 2026-11-25T03:00:00Z. Acceptance criteria target: 95th < 350 ms, 99th < 700 ms (we will populate the exact token-latency mapping in the addendum). Runbook & canary: prewarm canary at T-2 hours at 15% traffic; rollback triggers documented. Link: https://redwood.app/runbooks/oceanic-inflight-shield

2) Commercial/Legal: Ben will prepare a 1-paragraph amendment confirming the temporary carveout, rollback conditions, and the DocuSign link. Expect DocuSign draft by 2026-08-02; please confirm sign-off by 2026-08-05 to meet your marketplace schedule. DocuSign link (placeholder): https://docusign.com/link/ABC123

3) Operational: Marcus to share a final minute-by-minute traffic CSV by 2026-08-01 (we received traffic-forecast.csv; please replace with the minute-level sample).

4) Risks & mitigation: we recommend toggling to a quantized model variant during the peak if we see tail inflation due to KV-cache churn. That will be part of the runbook and prewarm test.

I’ll follow up with the formal addendum language and attach the updated capacity report once Ben and Legal sign off.

— Lauren
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: capacity_report_Q2.pdf, traffic-forecast.csv
